citation.title: Cluster-Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data

standing_assumptions:
The article is Aronow, Samii and Assenova, ‘Cluster–Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data’, Political Analysis 23:564–577 (2015). Printed page = PDF page + 563 (printed p. 566 is PDF p. 3). Everything quoted below and in the targets was read from the rendered page images (staged/pages/p-NN.png, checked against 200–300 dpi renderings of staged/main.pdf). Primes are transposes. The paper writes $\epsilon_d$ for the population residual and $e_d$ for the fitted (sample) residual; the two are different objects throughout.
(S1) Sampling and dyads, p. 566 (PDF p. 3): “Begin with a large population from which we take a random (i.i.d.) sample of units, with the sample members indexed by $i = 1, ..., N$ and grouped into $D = \binom{N}{2} = N(N-1)/2$ dyads. Pairs of unit indices within each dyad map to dyadic indices, $1, ..., D$, through the index function $d(i,j) = d(j,i)$, with an inverse correspondence $s(d(i,j)) = \{i,j\}$, and we assume no $d(i,i)$ type dyads.”
(S2) Regression and estimand, p. 566: “Consider a linear regression of $Y_{d(i,j)}$ on a $k$-length column vector of regressors $X_{d(i,j)}$ (which includes the constant): $$Y_{d(i,j)} = X'_{d(i,j)}\beta + \epsilon_{d(i,j)},$$ where $\beta$ is the slope that we would obtain if we could fit this model to the entire population, allowing for possible non-linearity in the true relationship between $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ and $X_{d(i,j)}$, and $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is the corresponding population residual.$^3$ To lighten notation, for the remainder of the discussion we use $d = d(i,j)$.” Footnote 3, p. 566: “If $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ is non-linear in $X_{d(i,j)}$, the population residual will itself vary in $X_{d(i,j)}$, which undermines inference that assumes that $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is independent of $X_{d(i,j)}$. The agnostic regression approach avoids such an assumption.”
(S3) Estimator, p. 566: “Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X_1 ... X_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$. The ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator is $$\hat\beta = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'Y,$$ with residual $e_d = Y_d - X'_d\hat\beta$.”
(S4) Dependence, boundedness and rank, p. 566: “Since the values of $Y_d$ and $X_d$ are determined by the characteristics of the units $i$ and $j$, $\epsilon_d$ and $\epsilon_{d'}$ for dyads containing either unit $i$ or $j$ are allowed to be correlated by construction. However, by random sampling of units, $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) = 0$ for all dyads that do not share a member. The number of pairwise dependencies between $i$ and $j$ for which $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) \ne 0$ is $O(N^3)$. Let the support for $X_d$ and $Y_d$ be bounded in a finite interval and assume the usual rank conditions on $\mathbf{X}$ (Chamberlain 1982; White 1984).”
(S5) Neighbouring dyads, p. 566 (repeated on p. 573): “$\mathcal{S}(d) = \{d' \ne d\} \cap \{d' : s(d) \cap s(d') \ne \emptyset\}$, the set of dyads other than $d$ that share a member from $d$.”
(S6) Repeated dyads, p. 567 (PDF p. 4): “Formally, suppose that for each dyad $d$ observations are indexed by $t = 1, ..., T(d)$, where the $T(d)$ values are fixed and finite. Let $(Y_{dt}, X'_{dt})$ represent the data for observation $t$ from dyad $d$, $$Y_d = \begin{pmatrix} Y_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ Y_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{and}\quad X_d = \begin{pmatrix} X'_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ X'_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix},$$ and $Y = (Y'_1 \ldots Y'_d \ldots Y'_D)'$ and $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 \ldots X'_d \ldots X'_D)'$, that is, the stacked $Y_d$ vectors and $X_d$ matrices, and let $\beta_r$ and $\hat\beta_r$ denote, respectively, the population slope and OLS estimator as defined above but now applied to the repeated dyads data.” In this case $X_d$ is a $T(d) \times k$ matrix and $e_d$, $\epsilon_d$ are $T(d)$-vectors.
(S7) Weighted observations, Appendix D, p. 575 (PDF p. 12): “Assume weighted directed dyad observations with weights finite and fixed; denote the weight for dyad $d$ as $w_d$. Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 ... X'_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$ and the matrix of weights as $\mathbf{W} = \mathrm{diag}\{w_1, \ldots, w_D\}$. Then, the weighted least squares estimator is $$\hat\beta_w = (\mathbf{X}'WX)^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}Y.$$” (In the display the $W$ and $X$ inside the inverse are set in italic, not bold; the meaning is $(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X})^{-1}$.) The paper does not define $\beta_w$.
(S8) Simulation design, p. 569 (PDF p. 6): “We suppose that population values obey the following: $$Y_{d(i,j)t} = \beta_0 + \beta_1|X_i - X_j| + \underbrace{\alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}}_{\epsilon_{d(i,j)t}}, \qquad (4)$$ where $Y_{d(i,j)t}$ is the $t$th observed outcome for the dyad that includes units $i$ and $j$, $X_i$, $X_j$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_j$, and $u_{d(i,j)t}$ are independent draws from standard normal distributions, and the compound error, $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}$, is unobserved. In the cross-sectional case, we only observe one outcome per dyad, so $t = 1$ for all observations (i.e., the $t$ subscript is extraneous for the cross-sectional case). In the repeated observations case, we have two observations per dyad, so $t = 1, 2$ for all dyads. We fix $\beta_0 = 0$ and $\beta_1 = 1$. We use OLS to estimate $\hat\beta_0$ and $\hat\beta_1$.”
(S9) Reading used by the validators (the audit's formalization of S1–S4; not printed as such). Each unit carries a characteristic $U_i$, the $U_i$ are i.i.d., and $(X_{d(i,j)}, Y_{d(i,j)}) = f(U_i, U_j)$ for one symmetric measurable $f$, with $X_d \in \mathbb{R}^k$ and $Y_d \in \mathbb{R}$ bounded. Hence collections of dyads on disjoint sets of units are independent, and all dyads have the same marginal law. $Q = \mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]$ is nonsingular (the ‘usual rank conditions’), $\beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ is the population least-squares projection, $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta$, so that $\mathrm{E}[X_d\epsilon_d] = 0$; nothing makes $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}] = 0$. The limit is $N \to \infty$. For repeated dyads the reading is $\beta_r = (\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d])^{-1}\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X_d\beta_r$; for weights, $\beta_w = (\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d])^{-1}\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta_w$.
Scope of the list. Targets are the paper's formal results (Lemma 1, Propositions 1–2, Corollaries 1–2, the logistic estimator of Appendix E) and every confirmed error whose correction changes a mathematical statement, a formula or a proof step: P018-E001, E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E007, N001, N003, N004, N006, N010. Two findings about the reported evidence rest on exact formal arguments and are targets for that formal content only: P018-E008 (the fitted random-effects benchmark has a covariance family that excludes the covariance of design (4)) and P018-E012 (‘an order of magnitude’ against the ratios of Table 1; the validator's evidence is itself a Lean proof). Not targets: P018-E009 (a mislabelled curve in SI Figure 4), E010 (sample counts), E011 (description of a regressor), E014 and E015 (wording and reference-list misprints), N008 (a cross-reference), which are findings about figures, data, reporting and bibliography with no mathematical statement to correct; P018-E013 and N002 (clarity notes); P018-N005 and N009 (not confirmed); P018-N007, N011, N012, N013 (out of scope). Of the headline claims, P018-H1 (Lemma 1, Proposition 1), H3 (Corollaries 1–2), H4 (Appendix E) and H5 (Proposition 2) are mathematical statements and are covered by P018-T26–T29, T14 and T16; H2 is the interpretive claim of valid inference under misspecification, whose formal content is T2, T4 and T8; H6–H10 are simulation and empirical claims.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Lemma 1, equation (2), with the second and third lines of equation (6) (Appendix A), the population $\Sigma$ of Appendix B and the conditional ‘meat’ of $V_r$ and $V_w$: an exact bounded, full-rank dyadic model in which the printed right-hand side is the zero matrix for every $N$ and the true variance is positive definite at leading order (the validator's construction; not in the paper)
canonical_claim.statement:
Model (validator's construction). Let $N \ge 3$ and let $Z_1, \ldots, Z_N$ be independent, each uniform on $[-1,1]$. For every unordered dyad $i<j$ put $$s_{ij} = Z_i + Z_j, \qquad X_{ij} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 + s_{ij} \end{pmatrix}, \qquad Y_{ij} = s_{ij}^2 .$$ Write $D = N(N-1)/2$, $h_{ij} = X_{ij}\epsilon_{ij}$ and $S = \sum_{i<j} h_{ij}$.
(a) [The model satisfies the paper's conditions] Units are i.i.d. and each dyad's data are a function of its two units; the second regressor lies in $[0,4]$ and $Y_{ij} \in [0,4]$. $$Q = \mathrm{E}[X_{12}X'_{12}] = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 14/3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \det Q = \tfrac23, \quad \mathrm{E}[X_{12}Y_{12}] = \begin{pmatrix} 2/3 \\ 4/3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_{12}Y_{12}] = \begin{pmatrix} 2/3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix},$$ so $\epsilon_{ij} = s_{ij}^2 - \tfrac23 \in [-\tfrac23, \tfrac{10}{3}]$, $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_{ij}] = 0$ and $\mathrm{E}[(2+s_{ij})\epsilon_{ij}] = 0$. The sample design matrix has rank 2 with probability one (the rows of dyads $\{1,2\}$ and $\{1,3\}$ have determinant $Z_3 - Z_2$). The conditional mean $\mathrm{E}[Y_{ij}|X_{ij}] = s_{ij}^2$ is not linear in $X_{ij}$.
(b) [The printed right-hand side is zero] $\epsilon_{ij} = (x_{ij} - 2)^2 - \tfrac23$, where $x_{ij} = 2 + s_{ij}$ is the second coordinate of $X_{ij}$; so $\epsilon_{ij}$ is a function of $\mathbf{X}$, and for all dyads $d, d'$, almost surely, $$\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}] = 0, \qquad \mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}] = 0 .$$ Hence the right-hand side of (2), the second and third lines of (6) and the $\Sigma$ of Appendix B are the $2\times2$ zero matrix for every $N$.
(c) [The true variance] With $$H = \mathrm{E}[h_{12}h'_{12}] = \begin{pmatrix} 28/45 & 56/45 \\ 56/45 & 3448/945 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Gamma = \mathrm{E}[h_{12}h'_{13}] = \begin{pmatrix} 4/45 & 8/45 \\ 8/45 & 632/945 \end{pmatrix},$$ $\det\Gamma = 1184/42525 > 0$ and $\Gamma_{11} > 0$ (so $\Gamma$ is positive definite), $\mathrm{E}[h_d] = 0$, and $\mathrm{E}[h_dh'_{d'}] = 0$ when $s(d)\cap s(d') = \emptyset$. For every $N \ge 3$, $$\mathrm{Var}(S) = DH + N(N-1)(N-2)\Gamma = \begin{pmatrix} \dfrac{2N(N-1)(2N+3)}{45} & \dfrac{4N(N-1)(2N+3)}{45} \\ \dfrac{4N(N-1)(2N+3)}{45} & \dfrac{4N(N-1)(158N+115)}{945} \end{pmatrix};$$ at $N = 3$ this is $\begin{pmatrix} 12/5 & 24/5 \\ 24/5 & 4712/315 \end{pmatrix} \ne 0$. So equation (2) is false in this model for every $N \ge 3$.
(d) [The discrepancy is of leading order] $\dfrac{N}{D^2}\mathrm{Var}(S) \to 4\Gamma$, and $V$ of equation (1), computed with the true $\mathrm{Var}(S)$, converges to $$V_* = 4Q^{-1}\Gamma Q^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 3664/315 & -592/105 \\ -592/105 & 296/105 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det V_* = \tfrac{4736}{4725} > 0,$$ a positive definite matrix, whereas substituting (2) into (1) gives the zero matrix.
(e) [Limit statements proved by the validator for this model] $\sqrt N(\hat\beta - \beta) \Rightarrow \mathcal{N}(0, V_*)$ and $N\hat V \overset{p}{\to} V_*$ with $\hat V$ of equation (3): the estimator converges to the true variance and not to the target that (2) gives.
(f) [Extensions] With $T(d) = 1$ for all $d$ (Corollary 1) and with $w_d = 1$ for all $d$ (Corollary 2) the middle factors of the printed $V_r$ and $V_w$ are built from the same conditional variances and covariances and are zero in this model.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Equation (1) and equation (2) as printed (p. 566): see P018-T26. Equation (6) as printed (p. 573): $$\mathrm{Var}\Big[\sum_{d=1}^{D}X_d\epsilon_d\Big] = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\sum_{d'=1}^{D}\mathrm{Cov}[X_d\epsilon_d, X_{d'}\epsilon_{d'}] = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\sum_{d'=1}^{D}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\} = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\Bigg(\underbrace{\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_d\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]\}}_{A} + \underbrace{\sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\}}_{B}\Bigg). \qquad (6)$$ $\Sigma$ of Appendix B (p. 573): $\Sigma = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\big(\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_d\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]\} + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\}\big)$. $\mathbf{X} = (X_1 ... X_D)'$ is the whole sample design (S3), so the conditioning is on all regressors. $\beta$, $\epsilon_d$: (S2), (S9). $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5). $\hat V$: equation (3), see P018-T27. $V_r$, $V_w$: P018-T28, P018-T29. Moments of the uniform law on $[-1,1]$: $\mathrm{E}[Z^{m}] = 0$ for odd $m$ and $1/(m+1)$ for even $m$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Parts (a)–(c) are exact for each $N$. For the limits in (d)–(e) the validator uses: (i) the count of ordered pairs of distinct dyads that share a member, $D \cdot 2(N-2) = N(N-1)(N-2)$; (ii) the exact decomposition $S = (N-1)\sum_{i=1}^{N} g(Z_i) + R_N$ with $g(z) = \mathrm{E}[h_{12}|Z_1 = z]$, $R_N = \sum_{i<j} r_{ij}$, $r_{ij} = h_{ij} - g(Z_i) - g(Z_j)$, $\mathrm{E}[r_{ij}|Z_i] = \mathrm{E}[r_{ij}|Z_j] = 0$, distinct $r$'s uncorrelated, $\mathrm{Var}(R_N) = D(H - 2\Gamma)$ and $\Gamma = \mathrm{E}[g(Z)g(Z)']$; (iii) the OLS identity $\sqrt N(\hat\beta - \beta) = Q_N^{-1}(\sqrt N/D)S$ with $Q_N = D^{-1}\sum_d X_dX'_d$; (iv) each entry of $Q_N$ has mean the entry of $Q$ and variance $O(1/N)$.
canonical_claim.note: P018-E001 is rated an error, Moderate (both validators confirm, each with its own exact witness; both re-runs upheld). Every number above was recomputed with exact rational integration when this list was fixed. The second validator's independent witness (runs/P018/validate/P018-E001/v2/artifact/derivation.md) is not required of the formalizer: $Z_i$ uniform on $[0,1]$, $X_{ij} = (1, Z_i+Z_j)'$, $Y_{ij} = (Z_i+Z_j)^2$, $\beta = (-5/6, 2)'$, $\mathrm{Var}(S)$ at $N=3$ equal to $\begin{pmatrix}3/20 & 3/20\\ 3/20 & 589/2520\end{pmatrix}$ and limiting covariance $\begin{pmatrix}229/315 & -74/105\\ -74/105 & 74/105\end{pmatrix}$. What is not established: that every misspecified model has an omission of order $N^3$, or any error in a reported number.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Lemma 1, equation (2), and equation (6) of Appendix A, corrected: the variance of the score sum in unconditional score moments, with the term that the printed conditional form omits
canonical_claim.location: p. 566 (PDF p. 3), eq. (2); p. 573 (PDF p. 10), eq. (6) and the $\Sigma$ of Appendix B
canonical_claim.statement:
Smallest repair for P018-E001, with the repeated/weighted prescription made explicit: “For the single-record model below, replace the conditional variance/covariance meat in (2), (6), and Appendix B by \Sigma_N^*=\sum_d(\mathrm E[X_dX_d'\epsilon_d^2]+\sum_{d'\in\mathcal S(d)}\mathrm E[X_dX_{d'}'\epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}]), which equals Var(sum_d X_d epsilon_d) under the stated projection orthogonality and disjoint-dyad independence. In $V_r$ and $V_w$, use the unconditional covariance of the total score, $\Omega_a=\operatorname{Var}(\sum_d h_d^a)$, for $a\in\{r,w\}$, with $h_d^r=X_d'\epsilon_d^r$ and, for one weighted record per dyad, $h_d^w=w_dX_d\epsilon_d^w$. For disjoint-dyad independent block scores, this is the sparse sum of unconditional score covariances. Uncentered score cross-moments may replace those covariances if every block score has mean zero; global projection orthogonality alone does not supply that condition. Alternatively add Var(E[sum_d X_d epsilon_d | bold X]) to the full conditional double sum, retaining any disjoint conditional terms unless their vanishing is justified. Update the associated expectation-identification argument with the proper normalization. Move the misplaced E in (2) in front of its braces.”
Corrected statement, with every hypothesis. Assume (S9): i.i.d. unit characteristics $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ ($N \ge 2$); $(X_{d(i,j)}, Y_{d(i,j)}) = f(U_i,U_j)$ with $f$ symmetric, $X_d \in \mathbb{R}^k$ and $Y_d$ bounded; $Q = \mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]$ nonsingular; $\beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$; $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta$. Put $h_d = X_d\epsilon_d$, $S = \sum_{d=1}^{D} h_d$ and $m_d = \mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]$. Then:
(i) $\mathrm{E}[h_d] = 0$ for every $d$, and $\mathrm{E}[h_dh'_{d'}] = 0$ whenever $s(d)\cap s(d') = \emptyset$.
(ii) [Equation (2), corrected] $$\mathrm{Var}\Big[\sum_{d=1}^{D}X_d\epsilon_d\Big] = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\Bigg(\mathrm{E}\big[X_dX'_d\epsilon_d^2\big] + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\big[X_dX'_{d'}\epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}\big]\Bigg) =: \Sigma_N^* .$$ Equivalently, in the printed form with $\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]$ replaced by $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d^2|\mathbf{X}]$ and $\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]$ by $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]$: $\Sigma_N^* = \sum_{d}\big(\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_d\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d^2|\mathbf{X}]\} + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\}\big)$.
(iii) [What the second line of (6) omits] $$\mathrm{Var}(S) = \sum_{d=1}^{D}\sum_{d'=1}^{D}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\} + M_N, \qquad M_N = \mathrm{Var}\big(\mathrm{E}[S|\mathbf{X}]\big) = \mathrm{Var}\Big(\sum_{d=1}^{D}X_dm_d\Big),$$ the first sum being $\mathrm{E}[\mathrm{Var}(S|\mathbf{X})]$. $M_N$ is positive semidefinite. The second equality of (6) holds if and only if $M_N = 0$; $m_d = 0$ almost surely for all $d$ is sufficient for $M_N = 0$, and $\mathrm{E}[X_d\epsilon_d] = 0$ alone is not (P018-T1).
(iv) [The sparse form of (2)] If $P_N$ denotes the right-hand side of (2) with the expectation of term $B$ placed before the braces as in (6), then $$\mathrm{Var}(S) - P_N = M_N + \sum_{(d,d'):\, s(d)\cap s(d') = \emptyset}\mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\} .$$
(v) [Closed form] With $H = \mathrm{E}[h_{d(1,2)}h'_{d(1,2)}]$, define $g(u)=\int h(u,v)\,\mu(dv)$ and $\Gamma=\mathrm{E}[g(U_1)g(U_1)']$ for every $N\ge2$, using the population score kernel $h(u,v)$ and unit law $\mu$. For $N\ge3$, also $\Gamma=\mathrm{E}[h_{d(1,2)}h'_{d(1,3)}]$. Thus $\Gamma$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and $$\Sigma_N^* = DH + N(N-1)(N-2)\Gamma, \qquad V = \frac{N}{D^2}Q^{-1}\Sigma_N^*Q^{-1} = Q^{-1}\Big(\frac{2}{N-1}H + \frac{4(N-2)}{N-1}\Gamma\Big)Q^{-1} \longrightarrow 4Q^{-1}\Gamma Q^{-1} .$$ Equation (1) is unchanged; its $\mathrm{Var}[\sum_d X_d\epsilon_d]$ is $\Sigma_N^*$.

Repeated and weighted scores, with every hypothesis for this prescription. Fix an integer $N\ge2$ and $k\ge1$, and let the units $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ be i.i.d. For every unordered dyad $d=\{i,j\}$ let $T(d)\in\{1,2,\ldots\}$ be deterministic and finite. Each record $x_{dt}\in\mathbb R^k$, $Y_{dt}\in\mathbb R$, $1\le t\le T(d)$, is a bounded measurable function only of $(U_i,U_j)$; the record functions and counts may vary with $d$ and $t$. Let $X_d\in\mathbb R^{T(d)\times k}$ have rows $x_{dt}'$, and let $Y_d\in\mathbb R^{T(d)}$ be the response block. For fixed real weights $w_{dt}$ put $W_d=\operatorname{diag}(w_{d1},\ldots,w_{dT(d)})$ (one weighted observation is $T(d)=1$ and $w_{d1}=w_d$). Put $A_r=\sum_d\mathrm E[X_d'X_d]$, $b_r=\sum_d\mathrm E[X_d'Y_d]$, $A_w=\sum_d\mathrm E[X_d'W_dX_d]$, and $b_w=\sum_d\mathrm E[X_d'W_dY_d]$; assume the relevant $A_a$ is nonsingular, and define $\beta_a=A_a^{-1}b_a$ for $a\in\{r,w\}$. Use $\epsilon_d^a=Y_d-X_d\beta_a$, $h_d^r=X_d'\epsilon_d^r$, $h_d^w=X_d'W_d\epsilon_d^w$, $S_a=\sum_dh_d^a$, and $\mu_d^a=\mathrm E[h_d^a]$. These bounded, finite-record scores are square-integrable; scores on disjoint dyads are independent. For either $a\in\{r,w\}$ the expected normal equations give $\mathrm E[S_a]=0$, and the exact identity is
$$\Omega_a:=\operatorname{Var}(S_a)=\sum_{d=1}^D\sum_{f=1}^D\mathrm E[h_d^a(h_f^a)']=\sum_{\substack{d,f:\ s(d)\cap s(f)\ne\varnothing}}\operatorname{Cov}(h_d^a,h_f^a)=\sum_{\substack{d,f:\ s(d)\cap s(f)\ne\varnothing}}\left(\mathrm E[h_d^a(h_f^a)']-\mu_d^a(\mu_f^a)'\right).$$
All these sums are over ordered pairs, including $d=f$. In particular,
$$\sum_{\substack{d,f:\ s(d)\cap s(f)\ne\varnothing}}\mathrm E[h_d^a(h_f^a)']=\Omega_a+\sum_{\substack{d,f:\ s(d)\cap s(f)\ne\varnothing}}\mu_d^a(\mu_f^a)'.$$
Consequently the sparse raw-moment sum equals $\Omega_a$ exactly when the displayed sum of products of block means is zero; $\mu_d^a=0$ for every $d$ is sufficient, while $\sum_d\mu_d^a=0$ alone is not. Without this cancellation, retain the centering products in the sparse sum, or retain all ordered pairs in the full raw-moment sum. With $L=\sum_dT(d)>0$, $H_r=A_r/L$, and $H_w=A_w/D$, the corresponding finite-$N$ covariance targets are $V_r=(N/L^2)H_r^{-1}\Omega_rH_r^{-1}$ and $V_w=(N/D^2)H_w^{-1}\Omega_wH_w^{-1}$, as in P018-T12. These are covariance identities; they do not by themselves assert consistency of a fitted-residual estimator.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Throughout, $N\in\mathbb N$, $N\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $k\ge1$, $D=N(N-1)/2$, and dyads are the unordered two-element sets $s(d)=\{i,j\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Define $\mathcal S(d)=\{f\ne d:s(d)\cap s(f)\ne\varnothing\}$. An overlap sum includes both the diagonal and all ordered pairs of distinct overlapping dyads. For square-integrable column vectors $A,B\in\mathbb R^k$, $\operatorname{Cov}(A,B)=\mathrm E[(A-\mathrm E A)(B-\mathrm E B)']$ and $\operatorname{Var}(A)=\operatorname{Cov}(A,A)$; expectations of vectors and matrices are entrywise. Conditional expectations and covariances given $\mathbf X$ mean conditioning on the sigma-algebra generated by the entire design matrix. Equalities between conditional expectations are almost sure. For the single-record model (S9), the unit law $\mu$ on a standard Borel space and the bounded measurable symmetric kernel $f=(x,y)$ are fixed as $N$ varies, with $X_{d(i,j)}=x(U_i,U_j)\in\mathbb R^k$ and $Y_{d(i,j)}=y(U_i,U_j)\in\mathbb R$; the paper includes a constant regressor. Let $h(u,v)=x(u,v)(y(u,v)-x(u,v)'\beta)$, $g(u)=\int h(u,v)\,\mu(dv)$, and $\Gamma=\int g(u)g(u)'\,\mu(du)$, so $\Gamma$ is defined even at $N=2$; its representation by two distinct overlapping sampled dyads requires $N\ge3$. At $N=2$, the overlapping-pair term in (v) is zero. The $V$ in (v) denotes the $N$-dependent covariance target in equation (1). The symbols $h_d,S,m_d,M_N,P_N,H,\Gamma,g,\Sigma_N^*$ are introduced by the correction. For repeated observations, $X_d$ instead denotes the block matrix with rows $x_{dt}'$; the superscript $a\in\{r,w\}$ distinguishes residuals at the stacked or weighted population projection from the single-record residual. The repeated/weighted quantities $A_a,b_a,\beta_a,h_d^a,S_a,\mu_d^a,\Omega_a,L,H_r,H_w$ and fixed weights are defined in the statement. Nonsingularity is required only for the population Gram matrices that are inverted. Equations (1), (2), (6), and the printed $\Sigma$ are recorded in P018-T26 and P018-T1; the repeated and weighted normalization is recorded in P018-T12.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: All of (i)–(v) are exact for each $N$ except the limit at the end of (v). Ingredients: the law of total covariance, $\mathrm{Cov}(h_d,h_{d'}) = \mathrm{E}\{X_dX'_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\} + \mathrm{Cov}(X_dm_d, X_{d'}m_{d'})$; $|\mathcal{S}(d)| = 2(N-2)$; the number of ordered pairs of distinct dyads sharing a member is $N(N-1)(N-2)$; $N/D = 2/(N-1)$ and $N\cdot N(N-1)(N-2)/D^2 = 4(N-2)/(N-1)$.
canonical_claim.note: Corrected statement for P018-E001 (error, Moderate). Repair cost per both validators: none (no new assumption, same estimand, same estimator). The operator-level form in (ii) is the second validator's wording of the same repair. Statement (iv) records the validators' caution that independence of disjoint dyads is unconditional, so the disjoint conditional covariances need not vanish term by term; no sign is claimed for that sum. The misplaced expectation in term $B$ of (2) is the separate finding P018-N001 (P018-T21). In the witness of P018-T1, $M_N = \mathrm{Var}(S)$ and the disjoint sum in (iv) is zero.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix B (proof of Proposition 1): exact bounded, full-rank model in which the printed mean condition, the printed limit $\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma]\to\Sigma$ and the printed dependence count for products of fitted residuals fail, while the conclusion of Proposition 1 holds; with the examples showing that convergence in probability of the inverse Gram matrix gives no moment control (the validators' constructions; not in the paper)
canonical_claim.statement:
Model. Let $N \ge 4$ and let $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ be independent with $\Pr(U_i = 1) = \Pr(U_i = -1) = \tfrac12$. For every unordered dyad $i<j$ put $X_{ij} = 1$ and $Y_{ij} = U_i + U_j$ ($k = 1$, intercept only). Then $\beta = 0$, $\epsilon_{ij} = U_i + U_j$, $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X} = D = N(N-1)/2 > 0$ in every sample, $Q = 1$, and all of $X$, $Y$, $\epsilon$ are bounded. Write $S = \sum_i U_i$, $\bar U = S/N$, $v_i = U_i - \bar U$.
(a) [Fit and target] $\hat\beta = 2\bar U$, $e_{ij} = v_i + v_j$, $|e_{ij}| \le 4$. $\Sigma = \mathrm{Var}(\sum_d\epsilon_d) = N(N-1)^2$ (which here also equals the printed conditional formula, since $X$ is constant and $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d] = 0$), and $V = (N/D^2)\Sigma = 4$.
(b) [Overlap identity] For every real array $(r_{ij})_{i<j}$, with $r_{ji} := r_{ij}$, $$\sum_{(d,d'):\, s(d)\cap s(d')\ne\emptyset} r_dr_{d'} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\Big(\sum_{j\ne i}r_{ij}\Big)^2 - \sum_{i<j}r_{ij}^2,$$ the left sum being over ordered pairs and including $d = d'$.
(c) [The meat, exactly] In every one of the $2^N$ samples, $\hat\Sigma = (N-2)(N-3)\big(N - S^2/N\big)$. Hence $\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma] = (N-1)(N-2)(N-3)$ and $$\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma] - \Sigma = (-4N+6)(N-1) \longrightarrow -\infty,$$ against the printed “$\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma] = \ldots \to \Sigma$” (p. 573). The normalized difference $(N/D^2)(\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma] - \Sigma) = (-16N+24)/(N(N-1)) \to 0$.
(d) [The printed mean condition fails] $\hat V = \hat\Sigma/D^2$, $\mathrm{E}[N\hat V] = \dfrac{4(N-2)(N-3)}{N(N-1)} \to 4$ and $$\mathrm{E}[\hat V - V] = \frac{4(N-2)(N-3)}{N^2(N-1)} - 4 \longrightarrow -4,$$ against the printed “(i) $\mathrm{E}[\hat V - V] \to 0$” and “uniform continuity implies $\mathrm{E}[\hat V - V] \to 0$”.
(e) [The printed pair of conditions is not sufficient] For the deterministic sequence $\hat V_N = 1$ and $V = 1$: $\mathrm{E}[\hat V_N - V] = 0$ and $\mathrm{Var}[N\hat V_N] = 0$, but $N\hat V_N - V = N - 1 \not\to 0$.
(f) [The conclusion of Proposition 1 holds here] $\mathrm{E}[S^4] = 3N^2 - 2N$, $\mathrm{Var}(S^2) = 2N(N-1)$, $N\hat V = \dfrac{4(N-2)(N-3)}{(N-1)^2}\big(1 - S^2/N^2\big)$ and $$\mathrm{Var}(N\hat V) = \frac{32(N-2)^2(N-3)^2}{N^3(N-1)^3} \longrightarrow 0,$$ so $N\hat V \overset{p}{\to} 4 = V$.
(g) [Fitted-residual products on disjoint units are correlated] For independent fair signs and real vectors $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{R}^N$, $$\mathrm{Cov}\big((a'U)(b'U), (c'U)(d'U)\big) = (a'c)(b'd) + (a'd)(b'c) - 2\sum_{l=1}^{N}a_lb_lc_ld_l .$$ For $N \ge 6$, $$\mathrm{Cov}(e_{12}e_{13}, e_{45}e_{46}) = \frac{16(N+6)}{N^3} > 0 \quad (= \tfrac{7}{16}\text{ at } N = 8),$$ whereas $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_{12}\epsilon_{13}, \epsilon_{45}\epsilon_{46}) = 0$. The quadruple $(d,d',d'',d''') = (\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{4,5\},\{4,6\})$ has $I_{d,d'} = I_{d'',d'''} = 1$, four distinct dyads, and $s(d)\cup s(d')$ disjoint from $s(d'')\cup s(d''')$, so it lies in none of the six cases listed on p. 574. At $N = 8$, $\mathrm{Cov}(e_{12}e_{13}, e_{14}e_{15}) = -\tfrac1{16} < 0$, so the covariance terms do not all ‘take positive values’.
(h) [Convergence in probability gives no moments] If $R_N = N$ with probability $1/N$ and $R_N = 1$ otherwise, then $R_N \overset{p}{\to} 1$, $\mathrm{E}[R_N] = 2 - 1/N \to 2$ and $\mathrm{Var}(R_N) = N - 3 + 3/N - 1/N^2 \to \infty$.
(i) [A bounded dyadic design with infinite inverse moment] Let $T_i$ be i.i.d. with density $t^{-2}$ on $[1,\infty)$, $Z_i = e^{-T_i}$, $X_{ij} = (1, Z_i + Z_j)'$ and $Q_N = \mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}/D$. Then $X_{ij}$ is bounded, $\det Q = 2\mathrm{Var}(Z_1) > 0$, the sample design has full rank almost surely for $N \ge 3$, $Q_N^{-1}\overset{p}{\to}Q^{-1}$, and for every $N \ge 3$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, $\mathrm{E}\|Q_N^{-1}\| \ge e^{2k}/(4k^N)$; hence $\mathrm{E}\|Q_N^{-1}\| = \infty$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Appendix B as printed: P018-T27 (conditions (i) and (ii), $\hat\Sigma$, $\Sigma$, the display $\mathrm{E}[\hat\Sigma]\to\Sigma$, the rewriting of $N\hat V$ with the indicator $I_{d,d'}$, $\Omega$, and the six cases). $\hat V$: equation (3). In this model $\hat\Sigma = \sum_{(d,d'):\,s(d)\cap s(d')\ne\emptyset}e_de_{d'}$ (ordered pairs, $d = d'$ included once). $\|\cdot\|$ in (i) is the operator norm; the bound uses the event $\{T_i \ge k\ \text{for all } i\}$, of probability $k^{-N}$, on which the lower-right entry of $Q_N$ is at most $4e^{-2k}$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (a)–(h) are exact for each $N$; (i) is exact for each $N$ apart from the limit $Q_N^{-1}\overset{p}{\to}Q^{-1}$. For (c): $\sum_{j\ne i}e_{ij} = (N-2)v_i$ and $\sum_{i<j}(v_i+v_j)^2 = (N-2)\sum_iv_i^2$, with $\sum_iv_i^2 = N - S^2/N$. For (g): $e_{ij} = \sum_l w_{ij,l}U_l$ with $w_{ij,l} = \mathbf{1}\{l\in\{i,j\}\} - 2/N$; each cross inner product is $-4/N$ and $\sum_l a_lb_lc_ld_l = 8/N^2 - 48/N^3$.
canonical_claim.note: P018-E006 is rated an error, Moderate: the printed proof of the paper's main consistency result does not prove it, and the conclusion survives by a replacement argument (P018-T4). Two validators, both re-runs upheld; the second validator's derivation (runs/P018/validate/P018-E006/v2/artifact/derivation.md) uses the same model and adds the value $-1/16$ in (g). The values $(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)$, $(-4N+6)(N-1)$, $7/16$ and $-1/16$ were re-enumerated over all $2^N$ samples ($N = 6, 8$) when this list was fixed. This is a counterexample to steps of the proof and not to Proposition 1: (f) shows the proposition's conclusion holds in the model. (i) does not show that $N\hat V$ itself has infinite moments; for that see P018-T19.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Proposition 1 with a corrected proof (replacement for Appendix B): consistency of $N\hat V$ for the target of equation (1) by a probability-limit argument, with the corrected Chebyshev conditions
canonical_claim.location: p. 567 (PDF p. 4), Proposition 1; pp. 573–574 (PDF pp. 10–11), Appendix B
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-E006), verbatim: “Replace Appendix B's moment-based proof by a probability-limit argument: retain N in the mean scaling; concentrate the population-score meat after multiplying it by N/D^2; use independence of collections determined by disjoint i.i.d. unit sets to count O(N^5) potentially dependent product pairs; bound fitted-residual substitution explicitly by a constant times ||hat beta-beta||+||hat beta-beta||^2; and combine the normalized meat with the sample inverse through continuity and O_p(1) multiplication. The derivation provides every step and defines the target using equation (1)'s unconditional score variance. Attribute finiteness of the fixed population inverse to rank, rather than boundedness.”
Corrected statement, with every hypothesis. Assume (S9): i.i.d. unit characteristics; $(X_d, Y_d) = f(U_i,U_j)$ with $f$ symmetric; $\|X_d\| \le C_X$ and $Y_d$ bounded; $Q = \mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]$ nonsingular; $\beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$; $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta$, so $|\epsilon_d| \le C_e$ for a finite $C_e$ and $\mathrm{E}[X_d\epsilon_d] = 0$. Let $z_d = X_d\epsilon_d$, $\delta_N = \hat\beta - \beta$, $$Q_N = \frac1D\sum_dX_dX'_d, \quad \mathcal{T}_N = \{(d,d') : s(d)\cap s(d')\ne\emptyset\}, \quad M_N(r) = \frac{N}{D^2}\sum_{(d,d')\in\mathcal{T}_N}X_dX'_{d'}r_dr_{d'}, \quad T_N = \mathrm{E}[M_N(\epsilon)],$$ $B_N = Q_N^{-1}$, $B = Q^{-1}$ and $V_N = BT_NB$. On samples where $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ is singular define $\hat\beta$ and $\hat V$ arbitrarily.
Conclusion: $$N\hat V - V_N \overset{p}{\to} 0 \quad\text{as } N\to\infty, \qquad V_N = \frac{N}{D^2}\,\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]^{-1}\,\mathrm{Var}\Big[\sum_{d=1}^{D}X_d\epsilon_d\Big]\,\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]^{-1},$$ that is, $V_N$ is the $V$ of equation (1), with $\mathrm{Var}[\sum_dX_d\epsilon_d]$ the unconditional score variance (P018-T2), and $\hat V$ is the estimator of equation (3). No moment of $Q_N^{-1}$ or of $N\hat V$ is used or asserted.
Corrected Chebyshev conditions (replacing (i)–(ii) of p. 573). For a scalar entry and a constant $V$, whenever the moments exist, $$\Pr(|N\hat V - V| > c) \le c^{-2}\big\{\mathrm{Var}(N\hat V) + (\mathrm{E}[N\hat V] - V)^2\big\},$$ so the sufficient pair is (i′) $\mathrm{E}[N\hat V - V]\to0$ and (ii) $\mathrm{Var}[N\hat V]\to0$; the printed (i) $\mathrm{E}[\hat V - V]\to0$ lacks the factor $N$ (P018-T3 (d), (e)). The replacement argument does not go through these conditions, because the moments need not exist (P018-T19).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Proposition 1 and equation (3) as printed: P018-T27. Equation (1): P018-T26. $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5); $\mathcal{T}_N$ is the set of ordered pairs of dyads that are equal or share a member, so $\hat\Sigma = \sum_{(d,d')\in\mathcal{T}_N}X_dX'_{d'}e_de_{d'}$ is the meat of (3). Norms are Euclidean / operator norms. $Q_N$, $\mathcal{T}_N$, $M_N$, $T_N$, $B_N$, $B$, $V_N$, $C_X$, $C_e$ are the validator's symbols.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Exact finite statements on which the replacement proof rests (validator's derivation, section 6). (L1) $|\mathcal{T}_N| = D(2N-3)$. (L2) $T_N = \dfrac{N}{D^2}\mathrm{Var}\big(\sum_dz_d\big) = \dfrac{N}{D^2}\sum_{(d,d')\in\mathcal{T}_N}\mathrm{E}[z_dz'_{d'}]$ and $\|T_N\| \le \dfrac{2(2N-3)}{N-1}C_X^2C_e^2 \le 4C_X^2C_e^2$. (L3) Each entry of $Q_N$ has mean the corresponding entry of $Q$, and at most $D(2N-3)$ of the $D^2$ covariances in its variance are nonzero, so its variance is at most $2C_X^4(2N-3)/D = O(1/N)$; the same count gives $D^{-1}\sum_dz_d = O_p(N^{-1/2})$, and on nonsingular samples $\delta_N = B_ND^{-1}\sum_dz_d$. (L4) A fixed unit belongs to at most $(N-1) + 6\binom{N-1}{2} = (N-1)(3N-5)$ pairs of $\mathcal{T}_N$; a pair of $\mathcal{T}_N$ involves at most 3 units; so at most $D(2N-3)\cdot3(N-1)(3N-5)$ ordered pairs of elements of $\mathcal{T}_N$ have intersecting unit sets, all others give independent products, and with $H_0 = C_X^2C_e^2$, $$\mathrm{Var}\big([M_N(\epsilon)]_{ab}\big) \le \frac{N^2}{D^4}\,2H_0^2\,D(2N-3)\,3(N-1)(3N-5) = O(N^{-1}).$$ (L5) $e_d = \epsilon_d - X'_d\delta_N$; $|e_de_{d'} - \epsilon_d\epsilon_{d'}| \le 2C_eC_X\|\delta_N\| + C_X^2\|\delta_N\|^2$; hence $\|M_N(e) - M_N(\epsilon)\| \le 4C_X^2\big(2C_eC_X\|\delta_N\| + C_X^2\|\delta_N\|^2\big)$. (L6) $N\hat V = B_NM_N(e)B_N$ and $$N\hat V - V_N = B_N[M_N(e) - T_N]B_N + (B_N - B)T_NB_N + BT_N(B_N - B).$$
canonical_claim.note: Corrected statement for P018-E006 (error, Moderate). Repair cost per both validators: none; the proof is replaced, not patched, and no new assumption is needed under the natural reading (S9). The paper's extra hypothesis that $X_d$ and $e_d$ ‘have bounded support with nonzero second moments and cross-moments’ is not used: boundedness of $\epsilon_d$ follows from bounded $X_d$, $Y_d$ and fixed $\beta$, and the validators record that a uniform bound on the fitted $e_d$ is neither implied by nor needed for this argument. $V_N$ depends on $N$; Proposition 1 writes $V$ for it. This target does not include a central limit theorem (P018-T8) or convergence of the finite-sample variance of $\hat\beta$ (P018-T20).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 4 and Supporting Information: the claim that design (4) with normal data ‘corresponds precisely to the assumptions of’ the fitted two-way normal random effects model. Exact covariance mismatch between design (4) and the model fitted in the replication archive, with an exact consequence for a model-based standard error (the validators' calculations; not in the paper)
canonical_claim.location: pp. 569–570 (PDF pp. 6–7), paragraph beginning ‘In the supplementary information’; Supporting Information p. 2; p. 572 (PDF p. 9), Conclusion; replication scripts 1 (line 86) and 2 (line 78)
canonical_claim.statement:
Setting. Dyads are the pairs $(i,j)$ with $1 \le i<j\le N$ (the scripts build them with the first endpoint the smaller index). Let $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ be the $D\times N$ first-endpoint and second-endpoint incidence matrices: row $(i,j)$ of $Z_1$ has a 1 in column $i$, row $(i,j)$ of $Z_2$ has a 1 in column $j$, all other entries 0; $Z = Z_1 + Z_2$.
(a) [Covariance of design (4)] With $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$ and $(\nu_{ij})_{i<j}$ independent with unit variances and $e_{ij} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{ij}$, $$\mathrm{Cov}(e_{ij}, e_{kl}) = |\{i,j\}\cap\{k,l\}| + \mathbf{1}\{(i,j) = (k,l)\},$$ i.e. the covariance matrix is $C = ZZ' + I$: 3 on the diagonal, 1 for distinct dyads sharing a unit, 0 for disjoint dyads.
(b) [Covariance family of the fitted model] The archive fits lmer(dY~dX + (1|dyad1) + (1|dyad2)), whose error is $\tilde e_{ij} = b_i + c_j + r_{ij}$ with $b$, $c$, $r$ mutually independent with variances $t_1, t_2, s \ge 0$. For distinct dyads $$\mathrm{Cov}(\tilde e_{ij}, \tilde e_{kl}) = t_1\mathbf{1}\{i = k\} + t_2\mathbf{1}\{j = l\},$$ i.e. the family is $W(t_1,t_2,s) = t_1Z_1Z'_1 + t_2Z_2Z'_2 + sI$.
(c) [Mismatch for every parameter value] For $N \ge 3$ and the dyads $(1,2)$ and $(2,3)$: $C$ has entry 1 and $W(t_1,t_2,s)$ has entry 0 for every $(t_1,t_2,s)$. Hence $C \ne W(t_1,t_2,s)$ for all $t_1,t_2,s$. For every $k<i<j$ the pair of dyads $\{(k,i),(i,j)\}$ has this mismatch; there are exactly $\binom{N}{3}$ such unordered pairs.
(d) [$N = 3$, dyads ordered $(1,2),(1,3),(2,3)$] $$Z_1 = \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad Z_2 = \begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}, \quad C = \begin{pmatrix}3&1&1\\1&3&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix}, \quad W(t_1,t_2,s) = \begin{pmatrix}t_1+t_2+s&t_1&0\\t_1&t_1+t_2+s&t_2\\0&t_2&t_1+t_2+s\end{pmatrix}.$$
(e) [Exact effect on a model-based variance, conditional mean correct] Take unit covariates $(X_1,X_2,X_3) = (0,1,3)$, so the dyad regressor $|X_i - X_j|$ is $(1,3,2)$ and the mean design is $F = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&3\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$; take $W = W(1,1,1)$. Then $$R = (F'W^{-1}F)^{-1} = \frac1{16}\begin{pmatrix}71&-27\\-27&15\end{pmatrix}, \qquad L = RF'W^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}19/16&-13/16&5/8\\-7/16&9/16&-1/8\end{pmatrix}, \qquad LF = I_2,$$ $$LCL' = \frac1{64}\begin{pmatrix}379&-135\\-135&67\end{pmatrix}.$$ The working model reports intercept variance $71/16$; the actual variance of the same estimator under $C$ is $379/64$; the ratio of reported to actual variance is $284/379 < 1$.
(f) [A lower bound that no fitted variance component can remove] If $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$ are i.i.d. $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, then $\bar\alpha = N^{-1}\sum_i\alpha_i$ has variance $1/N$ and is independent of $(\alpha_i - \bar\alpha)_i$, and $e_{ij} = 2\bar\alpha + (\alpha_i - \bar\alpha) + (\alpha_j - \bar\alpha) + \nu_{ij}$. Write the response vector as $y = y^c + 2\bar\alpha\mathbf{1}$ with $y^c$ independent of $\bar\alpha$. For every intercept estimator with $\hat\beta_0(y + c\mathbf{1}) = \hat\beta_0(y) + c$ for all real $c$ and finite variance, $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_0(y)) = \mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta_0(y^c)) + \frac4N \ge \frac4N,$$ which is $1/5$, $2/25$, $1/25$, $2/75$ at $N = 20, 50, 100, 150$.
(g) [Repeated observations] Adding an independent effect for each dyad (the term (1|dyads) of script 1, line 160) leaves the fitted covariance between an observation of dyad $(1,2)$ and an observation of dyad $(2,3)$ equal to 0, against 1 under (4).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Equation (4): (S8). As printed, pp. 569–570: “Specifically, we compare OLS with dyadic cluster robust standard errors to a two-way random effects model that incorporates normal random effects for each of the $N$ units (Gelman and Hill 2007). The data-generating process captured above (i.e., expression 4 with normal data) corresponds precisely to the assumptions of a two-way normal random effects model, and so it is no surprise that we find this model to be more efficient than OLS and to produce consistent standard errors.” The fitted formula is quoted from the authors' replication scripts (staged/code/dataverse-OMJYE5-v2.0-original), as recorded by both validators, who also checked lme4's actual random-effects design matrix: the two grouping terms give independent effect vectors even when the same numeric label occurs in both. In (e), $W^{-1} = \frac1{21}\begin{pmatrix}8&-3&1\\-3&9&-3\\1&-3&8\end{pmatrix}$; the estimator is $Ly$ (generalized least squares with the working covariance $W$).
canonical_claim.note: P018-E008 is rated an error, Moderate. It is a finding about the simulation benchmark (the code fits a model other than the one the text describes), included because it rests on an exact formal counterexample; (a)–(e) are in both validators' derivations, (f)–(g) in the first validator's (v1, sections 6 and 8), and both re-runs upheld. The matrices in (d)–(e) were recomputed exactly when this list was fixed. Not established: an asymptotic statement about the REML standard errors actually fitted (the components in (e) are fixed at 1, not estimated), a 25–30% shortfall at every $N$, or any change to the efficiency ordering. The translation-equivariance used in (f) holds for OLS and, per the validator, for a REML fit with a translation-invariant choice of optimizer; the target states it as a hypothesis on the estimator.
